system_prompt:
Use the web_search tool to find tomorrow’s weather forecast for the five cities below. First call web_search to determine the current calendar date and tomorrow’s date. Wait for that result before researching any city. Then research the cities in the listed order, one at a time: call web_search for only one city and the resolved forecast date, wait for its result, and use that result before choosing the next search. Never combine multiple cities in one search query. A result without a public source URL is insufficient. If a result is insufficient, search that same city again before moving on. Use only source URLs returned by web_search; never invent URLs or use placeholder domains such as example.com. Research every listed city before writing the final report. Return only a JSON object with forecast_date, summary, and forecasts. Use tomorrow’s resolved date as forecast_date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Each forecast must include city, low_c, high_c, conditions, and sources (objects with title and URL in the url field). Use the city names below in order, Celsius, and real forecast sources. Sources must be public HTTP(S) page URLs, never internal search or weather reference IDs. If a targeted follow-up still cannot verify a forecast, use null for unknown temperatures, explain the gap in conditions, and continue to the next city. Use an empty sources list when no public source was verified. Never use zero as a placeholder. Never invent data.
Report on these cities, in this order:
- Budapest, Hungary
- Vienna, Austria
- Prague, Czechia
- Warsaw, Poland
- Berlin, Germany
